note: Returning-visitor ids say whom a line fits: ret-any-* for any visitor (advisors and lobbyists included), ret-<club>-* only for a visitor who is that club's spokesperson. No line says whether the paper was signed or refused last time, how many times it has come, or anything about a mood; no office word, so every line reads true in every office. Away lines claim nothing that might not have happened (no visitors, no mood).

returning.text: The same paper as before. It has been ironed.
The same paper. The visitor hopes you have changed instead.
Back again. Cuthbert has filed it under AGAIN.
This paper has been here before. It knows the way.
Returned with a copy of itself, in case.
The same request, now with a covering letter about the request.
Back again, and this time all of it is underlined.
Word for word as before. They practised on the stairs.
Gwendolyn has opened a file for this one, then a second file.
Here once more, with the same words, said more slowly.
A fresh envelope. The words inside are not fresh.
Back again. They have brought their own chair.
The paper is back, and so is its paperclip, which looks tired.
The request is the same. The handwriting is neater.
Returned, unchanged, with a note pinned on: STILL ASKING.
Back again, by appointment. They made the appointment.
They have heard you like ribbons. There is one round it now.
Back again. Your portrait in the hall seems to know them.
Back again, at exactly the same time as last time.
This visit has been logged in a notebook, with the time.
The same paper, and a fresh flask.
Returned on the dot. The 7:02 could learn from this.
Back again. There is a footnote now, and it has a footnote.
Back again, with the timetable of their next visit attached.
Back again. The paper has spent the week in a shop window.
The paper has been polished. So has the bell.
The same paper, rearranged slightly for better presentation.
Back again, in a frame, lit from below.
Back again. Till's Teas has sent a cup with it, and a reminder.
Returned in tissue paper, with a bow tied at a careful angle.
Back again, with the same pumpkin and a firmer tone.
The paper has been entered for a rosette in the meantime.
Back again, wearing last year's rosette for luck.
Back again. They have weighed the paper, for fairness.
Back again. The pumpkin waits in the corridor, politely.
Here again, having waited as patiently as a seed.
Back again, humming the request under their breath.
The request has since been arranged for tuba.
The same request, now with a second verse.
Back again. The request has been rehearsed and is now in tune.
A cornet waits in the corridor, in case the answer needs music.
The paper is back, written a little louder.
Back again, so quietly you almost missed it.
The paper came back under the door without a sound.
They have been sitting outside, as patient as a float.
Back again. They have not said a word, which is how you know.
They waited by the water cooler, as if it were a pond.
Back again, cast gently onto the desk from the door.
Back again, carried in on a breeze they brought with them.
The paper has a tail on it now, for steadiness.
Back again. They have opened your window, just in case.
The paper arrived slightly before they did.
Back again, the paper folded into something that very nearly flies.
Back again, as hopeful as the first windy day of spring.
The paper has been trimmed to a perfectly even edge.
Back again. The margins have been measured, twice.
Your pens are now in a straight line. They did that while waiting.
Back again, with the corners squared off.
The paper has been clipped since. Only the parts that stuck out.
Back again. They have checked that your desk is level. It is not.

away.text: The clock chimed the hours without you. It managed.
Cuthbert sorted the drawer FOR FURTHER STUDY, then studied that.
Gwendolyn balanced the books, then, having time, balanced them again.
Rodney dusted your portrait. Twice, from the good side.
Your parking space waited for you. Nobody else dared.
The ministries collected without you. Gwendolyn says they barely noticed.
Rodney wrote a speech for your return. It is mostly about you.
A committee watered the office plant, after a short meeting.
Your photograph kept an eye on things. It reports nothing.
Your chair was kept warm by a cushion with your name on it.

captions.text: Mayor of Dithering-on-the-Dawdle, unopposed. The other candidate went to the wrong hall.
Governor of Upper Wobbling. A mahogany desk, a green lamp, and Pruella, near lunch.
President. A walnut desk, three telephones, and Mildred, who liked one of the last three.
You serve on, as Acting. Rodney has had that word painted very small on the door.
Every district held. Rodney is having the result framed, and then the frame.
A Quiet Term. Nothing new this time. The clock has been told, and took it well.
